name: Gail K. Boudreaux

President; Executive Vice President, UnitedHealth Group

background_rationale: Spent more than three decades running health insurance businesses at Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois/HCSC and UnitedHealthcare, starting as a management trainee and rising through operating roles to CEO.

notable.summary: Anthem renamed its holding company Elevance Health, with Boudreaux saying the name better reflected the business it had become.
Boudreaux announced Elevance would acquire CareBridge, a home- and community-based care management company, to expand its Carelon services division.
Boudreaux described 2026 as a year of execution and repositioning, as Elevance guided to a low-single-digit revenue decline and targeted a return to 12% EPS growth in 2027.
Boudreaux said Elevance would exit additional Medicaid markets over the next 12 to 18 months where it did not see a path to sustainable performance.

personal_story.hook: Before running a health insurer, Gail Boudreaux's first full-time job was playing professional basketball in France.
personal_story.summary: Boudreaux grew up in Chicopee, Massachusetts, the daughter of a machinist and a homemaker, playing pickup sports in neighborhood parks with her older brother. At Dartmouth she was a 6-foot-2 center, a three-time Ivy League Player of the Year and the program's all-time leading scorer and rebounder. After graduating in 1982 she spent a year playing professionally in Versailles, France, without speaking the language. A summer internship at Aetna led to a spot in its management training program in 1983, the start of a career in health insurance that took her to the top of UnitedHealthcare and then Anthem.
